audit_scope.description: This audit covers both EL and CL logic: Fulu fork transition, proposer lookahead (EIP-7917), dynamic blob parameters (EIP-7892), blob base fee reserve pricing (EIP-7918), and their interfaces.

out_of_scope_reasons.Mainnet/Testnet Testing: All testing should be done on local forks of testnet or mainnet
out_of_scope_reasons.Pricing Oracles (Third-party): Incorrect data supplied by third party oracles (oracle manipulation/flash loan attacks are in-scope)
out_of_scope_reasons.Third-party Smart Contracts: Any testing with third-party systems and applications is prohibited
out_of_scope_reasons.Websites/Web Applications: Not in scope for smart contract bug bounty
out_of_scope_reasons.Test Files: Impacts on test files and configuration files unless stated otherwise
out_of_scope_reasons.Configuration Files: Impacts on test files and configuration files unless stated otherwise

bug_bounty_scope.notes: The subgraph files describe Ethereum protocol-level EIPs (Fulu fork, EIP-7917, EIP-7892, EIP-7918) rather than Sherlock smart contracts. The Sherlock bug bounty scope is provided as context but the analyzed specs are Ethereum consensus/execution layer specifications.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer (Validator) via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (beacon_block topic) - block proposals with blob KZG commitments
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any validator can propose blocks. Proposers are selected deterministically but may be malicious. Block content including blob commitments must be fully validated against dynamic limits.

trusted_external_entities.name: Peer Beacon Node via P2P Network
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Unauthenticated P2P peers may send invalid blocks, malformed execution payloads, or blocks exceeding blob limits. All data requires full validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Remote Peer via P2P Discovery
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P peer discovery (ENR fork digest advertisement)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Remote peers attempting connection may be on a different blob parameter schedule or fork version. Fork digest comparison is the primary defense against network partition.

trusted_external_entities.name: Execution Layer Client via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: EL client is co-located and authenticated via JWT. However, EL responses (payload validity, state roots) must still be cross-checked. A compromised or buggy EL client could return incorrect validation results.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Producer via Block Construction
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block producers set header values that feed into reserve price calculations. Validators must independently verify excess_blob_gas using the modified calc_excess_blob_gas formula.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P (devp2p)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers provide blocks for validation. The excess_blob_gas header field must be recalculated locally and compared; any mismatch results in block rejection.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: CL sends execution payloads for verification via JWT-authenticated Engine API. Payload content (including blob gas fields) must still be validated against EL state.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: Blob KZG commitment count must be validated against get_blob_parameters(epoch).max_blobs_per_block. Block proposer may include excess commitments to exploit dynamic limit miscalculation.
All received blocks must undergo full validation including execution payload verification and dynamic blob limit checks. Peer may send blocks with invalid blob counts or corrupted execution payloads.
Fork digest must encode both fork version and blob parameters (via XOR). Peers on different blob schedules must be rejected. Collision resistance of truncated XOR hash is assumed sufficient.

EL validation result is trusted for execution state transitions but CL must independently validate CL-specific fields (blob commitments, blob limit). JWT authentication ensures channel integrity but not content correctness of a buggy EL.
The excess_blob_gas header value must be independently recalculated using the modified calc_excess_blob_gas with reserve price logic. Header values cannot be trusted from the block producer.
All block header fields including excess_blob_gas must be recalculated and verified. Peer blocks with mismatched excess_blob_gas (especially around reserve/normal mode transitions) must be rejected.

Execution payload forwarded by CL must be validated against EL state including reserve price logic for excess_blob_gas. JWT ensures authentic CL source but payload originates from untrusted block proposer.
